full_judgment:
2. The suit brought by the 2 plaintiffs. Kashem Sarder and Sumangal Biswas, on 23.11.1979, is for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with their possession in the suit lands which have been described in the plaint schedule as measuring 3.30 acres out of 9.79 acres of S.A. Khatian No.19/1 of Mouja Chakhail-Machalia under P.S. Batiagatha, District Khulna. 

 10. As to maintainability of the suit which has not been considered by either of the courts below it appears that serious complicated question of title are involved in the suit. There in nothing on record to show as to how defendant no. I Hazarilal acquired the life-interest of Sarathi and Shouravi, or in other words, 9-annas interest in the suit properties as claimed in the plaint. The plaint itself is silent as to how Hazarilal and after him the plaintiffs got or entered into possession of the suit properties; in order so make up the deficiency, a new case beyond pleading has been attempted to be made out by introducing from the mouth of Hazarilal a story of frocible ouster by him of the transfers from the 3 widows. Further, the more, the plaintiffs' Kabala Ext. I shows that they purchased Hazari's interest as inherited by him from his father and also devolved upon him as reversioner from Kumudini, whereas the plaintiffs have claimed the interest enjoyed by the other 2 widows as life interest and transferred by them to Nerode and Mohesh. The question of legal necessity behind the transfers by the widows is yet a complicated question of title involved. Again, the plaintiffs Kabala Ext.1 speaks of transfer in their favour of 3.30 acres out of 10.97 acres of lands, where the area described in the plaint schedule in 9.97 acres. It may be mentioned, however, that the total area of the holding belonging to the original holders named Rajani, Nimchand and Dharmachand as recorded in C.S. Khatian No.19 comprising 2 plots No. 453(75) and No. 454(10.04) was 10.79 acres. During S.A. operations, the entire plot No.453 and 9.04 acres out of plot No.454 with a total area of 9.79 acres have been recorded in S.A. Khatain No.19/1 and the remaining 1100 acre out of plot No.454 remains unexplained. Having purchased from the entire 10.79 acres of the properties, i.e., the 2 entire plots, the plaintiffs have brought the suit leaving aside the aforesaid 1.00 acre of land. I cannot but, therefore agree with Mr. Matlub Ahmed. Serious complicated question of title are involved in the suit. It has been clearly laid down in the case of Rafizuddin Ahmad Vs. Mongla Barmon & ors reported in 43 DLR (AD) 215 that if the dispute involved complicated question of title the plaintiff must establish hid title, by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. Simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title. In this case the plaintiffs alleged title is not clear and they do not appear to have prima facie title to the lands claimed in the suit. True, the courts below have not properly discussed the evidence adduced by the parties on possession of the land; but in view of the findings I have arrived at, the discussion of evidence on possession is simply redundant. Because, if the suit lands are allowed to remain vague and unspecified and the plaintiffs fail to prove their prima facie title there to, the suit itself fails for non-maintainability.
